notes.b1/j1/F-r1: Clean four-block sandbox with counts, undo, keys and good mobile layout, but opens empty and visually plain.
notes.b1/j1/Q-r1: Textured pixel blocks, sky, clouds and a pre-built landscape with nine block types make it the most polished and inviting, with a wrapping mobile palette.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Feature-rich with Place, Erase, Pick and Fill tools, but the block look is flat and the toolbar is cramped.
notes.b1/j1/Q-r2: Attractive beveled blocks and a starter scene with ten palette slots, undo and a status line, and it works well on mobile.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Works with a Generate button but looks dim, with grid artifacts and tiny labels, and starts as an empty dark grid.
notes.b1/j1/F-r2: Tidy counters per block type and a hint line, with the world starting empty and plain.
notes.b1/j2/Q-r2: Pre-built 32x32 scene with bevelled blocks, 9 types, undo, drag-place; dark empty sky is plain and tiny status text.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: Works with a Generate button, but opens empty with flat colors and stray grid-line artifacts, little visual character.
notes.b1/j2/F-r2: Clean toolbar with per-block counts, but only four blocks, empty start and faint checkerboard with artifact lines.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: Fill, pick and place/erase modes with 9 block types and a ground pre-filled, but plain look and grid lines bleed through blocks.
notes.b1/j2/Q-r1: Textured blocks, sky, clouds and a generated landscape with trees and water; polished, responsive, new-world and undo controls.
notes.b1/j2/F-r1: Neat labelled toolbar with key hints and responsive wrapping, but only four blocks and an empty board with little visual interest.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Working 32x32 sandbox with 8 blocks, erase, undo and a Generate button, but opens as a blank dark grid with a tiny, low-contrast toolbar.
notes.b1/j3/F-r2: Clean 4-block palette with counts and status text, but the empty checkered world has little visual appeal and few blocks.
notes.b1/j3/Q-r2: Opens with a pre-built scene of ground, tree, house and water, 3D-bevelled blocks, 9 palette items, and a layout that works well on mobile.
notes.b1/j3/F-r1: Tidy, polished toolbar with keyboard hints, but the empty world gives no first impression and the palette is small.
notes.b1/j3/A-r1: Many tools (Place, Erase, Pick, Fill, Grid) and a starter ground layer, but blocks are plain, it has no sky, and the mobile toolbar is cramped.
notes.b1/j3/Q-r1: Best looking: textured pixel blocks, sky with clouds, a generated terrain with trees and water, a New world button, and a clean mobile layout.
notes.b2/j1/F-r3: Top-down 32x32 grid with stacked heights and only three block types; works but the mobile toolbar is clipped and the empty beige board is bland.
notes.b2/j1/Q-r3: Textured side-view 32x32 world with a pre-built landscape, ten blocks, undo/reset; attractive though the board runs past the desktop fold.
notes.b2/j1/A-r3: Clean empty dark grid with a sidebar palette, autosave and counters; plain visually and the mobile layout pushes the palette below the board.
notes.b2/j1/Q-r4: Polished isometric 3D 32x32 voxel terrain with place/erase modes, nine blocks and new-terrain; clearly the most impressive and responsive.
notes.b2/j1/A-r4: Flat empty 32x32 grid with eight swatches and save; functional but minimal, with uneven grid lines on mobile.
notes.b2/j1/F-r4: Tidy dark grid with per-block counts, erase tool and undo/clear, but only four block types and the desktop footer is cut off.
notes.b2/j2/Q-r4: True isometric 3D 32x32 world with terrain, nine materials, place/erase/undo and a responsive layout; clearly the richest and most block-like.
notes.b2/j2/A-r4: Top-down flat grid with eight colours and undo/save, but it starts blank and reads as a paint grid rather than blocks.
notes.b2/j2/F-r4: Only four materials on a dark empty grid with counts and a two-step clear; tidy but sparse and visually flat, and the footer is cut off on desktop.
notes.b2/j2/A-r3: Eight materials, a side palette, autosave and a block cap, but a dark empty 2D grid with little sense of building; the mobile palette pushes controls below the fold.
notes.b2/j2/Q-r3: Side-view 32x32 world with textured blocks, preloaded terrain and tree, ten tools, and a phone layout that works.
notes.b2/j2/F-r3: Top-down grid with stacking to height 6 and keyboard shortcuts, but only three materials and a blank start with no depth cue.
notes.b2/j3/A-r4: Flat top-down 32x32 painter with 8 colors and save; works but looks like a plain pixel grid, empty start, and the mobile grid lines render unevenly.
notes.b2/j3/F-r4: Polished dark 32x32 grid with counts and shortcuts but only four kinds, empty dark canvas and the desktop footer is cut off at 800px.
notes.b2/j3/Q-r4: Isometric 3D 32x32 voxel world with generated terrain, 9 block types, place/erase/undo, and a layout that fits desktop and phone.
notes.b2/j3/F-r3: Top-down column stacking with a height cap of 6 and clear hints is sound but visually bare with only three block types.
notes.b2/j3/A-r3: Clean sidebar with 8 blocks, autosave and block count, but it is a flat empty grid with no sense of building.
notes.b2/j3/Q-r3: Textured side-view 32x32 sandbox with pre-built terrain, tree, 10 tools and good mobile layout; reads as a Minecraft-like builder.
